name: blender
label: Blender 4.x (Principled BSDF)

maps.notes: Colour space Non-Color. Blender applies the sRGB transfer curve to anything left as Color, which makes a roughness map look plausible and shade wrong.
Non-Color, +Y (OpenGL), which is Blender's own convention: no green-channel flip needed.
Non-Color. Cycles needs subdivision or Adaptive Subdivision for this to do anything, and the displacement method must be set to Displacement or Both rather than Bump Only.
Principled BSDF has no ambient occlusion input. Mixing this into Base Color is an artist's decision, not an exporter's.
Blender expects straight alpha; set the material's blend mode deliberately, since the 4.x defaults changed.
sRGB. Emission Strength is a material value and can exceed 1.

notes: The snippet sets colourspace_settings per node, which is the step people skip: a roughness map left as Color renders, and renders wrong.
For a tiled material, leave the image texture's extension as REPEAT and set the mapping scale, rather than editing UVs.
Coat, Sheen and Anisotropic exist on the 4.x Principled BSDF for car paint, velvet and brushed metal; nothing in this export fills them.
The classic mistake for this target is forgetting Non-Color on the data maps, so the snippet sets it for every node it creates.
